standard_prerequisites.name: Complex attached to a simplicial object and acyclicity
standard_prerequisites.statement: The chain complex s(E) associated to a simplicial object, and the criterion that acyclicity follows from a contracting homotopy.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion and the means of proof (source lines 3879, 3928-3930).

standard_prerequisites.name: The extension map on the simplex category
standard_prerequisites.statement: The operation sending alpha : [n] -> [k+1] to alpha' : [n+1] -> [k+1] agreeing with alpha on [n] and taking the top element to k+1.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is defined at the start and used to build the homotopy (source lines 3883-3900).

core_obligations: Define the extension operation on simplex maps and analyse the induced maps: introduce alpha' extending alpha by the top element and determine how the components of E behave according to whether the image of alpha is [k] or [k+1] (source lines 3883-3900).

Construct the contracting homotopy: define maps h_n : E_n -> E_{n+1} componentwise from the extension operation and compute the composite with the differential to verify the homotopy identity, which requires the sign (-1)^(n+1) (source lines 3900-3928).
Conclude acyclicity: exhibit the system h'_n = (-1)^(n+1) h_n and conclude that E is acyclic (source lines 3928-3930).

proof_roadmap.step: Define alpha' and analyse the induced maps on the components of E.
Build the maps h_n and verify the homotopy identity with the correct sign.
Conclude that the complex is acyclic.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-homology-extension at source lines 3873-3880: for an abelian category, an object A and an integer k, the complex s(E) attached to the object E constructed in the author's extension lemma is acyclic. The proof at source lines 3882-3931 is an explicit contracting homotopy. It first defines an extension operation on the simplex maps into [k+1], by extending a map on [n] to [n+1] fixing the new top element, then analyses how the components of E behave according to the image of the map, constructs a system of maps h_n between consecutive degrees, verifies the required identities with the differential (where the sign (-1)^(n+1) is needed) and concludes acyclicity by exhibiting the homotopy. The final sentence names a result of the Homology chapter as an alternative way to conclude; that reference is declared as a source pointer from the project tag list, while the counted argument exhibits the homotopy explicitly and uses nothing outside the retained spans.
